name: Sree Ramar Temple
significance: A Rama temple at Changi Village founded in 1946 by Ram Naidu of the British Indian Army, on a site the British Army donated at the end of the Second World War, and long patronised by Hindu workers at the nearby RAF Changi base. It grew from a shrine at the foot of a tree; granite images were installed in newly built sanctums during the 1991 rebuilding, and displaced shrines were absorbed into it in 1999.

name: Sri Senpaga Vinayagar Temple
significance: A Ganesha temple on Ceylon Road in Katong whose origins go back to the 1850s and a modest attap-roofed shelter raised under the Ceylonese Tamil pioneer Ethirnayagam Pillai. The Singapore Ceylon Tamils' Association bought the land in 1923 and remains its keeper; a concrete temple was completed in 1929 and a full rebuilding in the late 1990s added a 21-metre raja gopuram, consecrated in 2003.
story: The temple is said to have begun where a statue of Vinayagar was found beside a pond, next to the chempaka tree — senpaga in Tamil — that gave the temple its name.

name: Sri Krishnan Temple
significance: The only Tamil temple in Singapore dedicated to Krishna together with Rukmini, begun in 1870 by the wealthy merchant Hanuman Beem Singh, who set images of the deities at the foot of a banyan tree to serve a growing Hindu population in the district. The main shrine was rebuilt in 1933 on donations from Naraina Pillai and Pakirisamy Pillai, in a classical Dravidian idiom following Agama Sastra, and has been renovated repeatedly since, most recently between 2016 and 2018.

name: Sri Layan Sithi Vinayagar Temple
significance: A Ganesha temple at the junction of Keong Saik Road and Kreta Ayer Road in Chinatown, built in 1925 by the Nattukottai Chettiar community with funding from the Chettiars of Tamil Nadu. It replaced an older attap-roofed temple near Singapore General Hospital, which had served hospital employees, Outram Prison staff and soldiers of the Sepoy Lines until the government acquired that land in 1920; its five-tier gopuram tapers to represent the five senses.

name: Sri Poyatha Moorthi Temple
significance: A Ganesha temple on Jalan Tukang Emas in Malacca, built in 1781 by Thavinayagar Chitty, leader of the Chitty community, on a plot the Dutch colonial government of Malacca granted him for a Hindu temple; the Dutch freehold grant supplies its date. A further altar within the temple is dedicated to Muruga.
